relevance_note: Single case report of a clinically and radiologically diagnosed child: "a final diagnosis of Infantile AD was established"; no GFAP testing ("Genetic evaluation was not performed in the present case").
method_note: Hand extraction from the case report; a small script assembled the JSON. One in-scope person (the unnamed five-year-old boy, label 'patient'), in scope by diagnosis of Alexander disease, not by a GFAP variant: genetic evaluation was not performed, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported (defined as patients with a GFAP variant) is null. The parents are mentioned only as informants (not tested, not stated affected; 'Patient's family history was found to be insignificant'), so they get no rows. Rodriguez D et al. and Goyal M et al. [7,8] are cited only as reports of infantile AD with normal head circumference, with no identifiable individual, so no rows. 'Haematological parameters were found to be normal' is a whole investigation; recorded as written (abnormal haematological parameters, excluded) without naming anything more specific. Normal head circumference recorded as macrocephaly excluded (D-27); the checklist item 'macrocephaly or megalencephaly' was also set excluded from the same statements. 'Progressive generalized weakness' was taken as observed for the checklist item 'limb weakness'; 'episodes of vomiting' as observed for 'recurrent vomiting'. Not used for the checklist: 'feeding difficulties' (not dysphagia), 'inability to speak' (not dysarthria), 'gait and postural abnormality' (not ataxia), 'cognitive abnormalities' (not stated as decline). Head circumference at birth was also stated normal ('normal at birth with standard birth weight and head circumference'); not made a separate row. Age at diagnosis is not stated (diagnosis made at the presentation as a five-year-old, but no age is tied to it). No contradictions found.
